intro: Picture a small resort, just a few units clinging to a Khao Kho hillside, where you open the balcony door in the morning to a green valley and layered mountain ridges right in front of you, air so cool you reach for a blanket to throw over your shoulders — Khao Kho Tree Top is a budget-friendly wooden-cabin stay in Khao Kho district, Phetchabun, built mainly around the "view" and the "cool air" rather than selling luxury or a full set of amenities · This isn't a big resort with a swimming pool or an all-out theme; it's a small, simple place that suits people who want to sleep with a quiet valley in view, near Pha Sorn Kaew and Khao Kho National Park · Prices are budget-friendly, starting at about ฿1,200/night in normal periods · In this review we've gathered the real guest reviews, both praise and complaints, and tell it to you straight before you decide to book

body.html: Who Khao Kho Tree Top is right for — to put it as briefly as possible, Khao Kho Tree Top is a small wooden-cabin resort on a Khao Kho hillside for people who "want to sleep with a valley view on a budget" rather than those chasing luxury or a full set of amenities · It's not an all-out themed resort with a castle, flower gardens, or an infinity pool, and it's not a hotel in Phetchabun town that's easy to reach from every direction · It's a simple place of just a few units perched on a high slope, facing out to a valley and layered mountain ridges, with cool air almost all year · From the real reviews on booking and international review sites, the picture is fairly consistent: the people this suits are couples wanting to escape the bustle and sleep somewhere quiet, small families looking for a light-on-the-wallet base for exploring Khao Kho, and nature-minded travelers who value the "view off the room" and the "cool air" more than in-room luxury · Another group that says they're happy are those who drive themselves and aren't expecting big-hotel service — they just want a clean bed, a good view, and good value · On the flip side, if you're someone who wants a luxurious room, a swimming pool, a buffet breakfast, or 5-star service, this may not be your answer, and you should look at the larger, higher-priced resorts on Khao Kho instead · Put simply, Khao Kho Tree Top leans on "good value and a good view" as its main selling point, traded against the simplicity of the place itself and service that isn't all-out — something worth knowing and making peace with right from the moment you book

Location and getting there — Khao Kho Tree Top is located at No. 216, Khao Kho subdistrict, Khao Kho district, Phetchabun province, on a hillside facing out toward the valley · The strength of the location is that it sits in the Khao Kho zone surrounded by popular attractions, especially Wat Pha Sorn Kaew, the highlight of Khao Kho, and Wat Phra Borommathat Kanchanaphisek (the famous mosaic temple), about 2 kilometers away according to booking-site information · It's also a not-too-far drive from Sri Dit Waterfall (about 7 kilometers), the Khao Kho viewpoints and Thung Samo, and the entrance to Khao Kho National Park · As for getting there, we have to say it straight: accommodation on Khao Kho generally suits people who drive themselves the most, because the sights are spread out across the hills and there's no convenient public transport · The resort sits on a slope you have to drive up; the final stretch of road is an uphill climb — an ordinary sedan can make it but should be driven carefully, especially when it's raining and the road can be slippery · A note from the real reviews: most of the signs are in Thai, and some foreign visitors say they found it a bit hard to find the way in, and the place is farther from the mosaic temple than they'd expected · So if you use a navigation app, we'd suggest pinning the resort's name accurately and allowing extra time for the drive up the hill

"The nights on the hillside are wonderfully cool, with thick enough blankets to stay warm without being too cold · Waking up and opening the balcony to a valley and layered ridges — worth every baht we paid. The one gripe is that all the signs are in Thai, so finding the way in at night was a bit of a struggle."

Room types and decor — Khao Kho Tree Top is a small place with just a few rooms and cabins. Booking-site information splits them into several types, including single, twin, triple rooms, and cabins (bungalow/chalet) that face the valley · A point reviews mention often is that many cabins look out onto "a valley and mountain ridges layered in tiers," which is the main charm of the place · The rooms keep it simple in a wooden-cabin style, not luxuriously decorated, and each unit has a private balcony or terrace for sitting and enjoying the view, which many guests say is where they spend the most time · One thing to understand is that most rooms rely on fans, because the air on Khao Kho is cool enough already, especially in the late rainy/early cool season when the nights get downright cold · The in-room kit covers the basics for a few nights' stay — a TV, electric kettle, a sitting corner, and an en-suite bathroom with shower, toiletries, and towels · One foreign reviewer put it bluntly: "all the room types are the same, the only difference is whether you're on the upper or lower floor", which reflects that this is a simple place rather than one with a range of room tiers · The upside is that when expectations line up, most people say they slept comfortably and warm enough with the blankets provided · For anyone sensitive about how new a room is, understand that the place is wooden cabins that have seen some use, so some details aren't as crisp as a brand-new hotel, and cleanliness and attention to detail score middling in some reviews

Facilities and surroundings — we have to say it straight: Khao Kho Tree Top is a small resort, so the facilities focus on the basics rather than going all out · From the information available, the place has free Wi-Fi, free parking, laundry service, and a garden in the common area to stroll and enjoy the view · What it doesn't have, and you should know this, is a swimming pool, a fitness center, or a spa like the bigger resorts · The real draw here isn't the in-house facilities but the hillside location overlooking the valley and ridges and the cool air that nature provides · The late rainy/early cool season (October–February) is when the atmosphere is at its best, with a chance to see mist drifting through the valley in the morning and cold that's just right · The resort sits among the trees and the quiet, suited to people who genuinely want to rest, not those who want entertainment or shops all around · For people who love the simple "cabin in the mountains" feel, this is the charm — but for those who want big-resort facilities, it may feel like too little on offer, which is reasonable given a price that's lower than many places on Khao Kho

Food and affiliated outlets — food is another area where you need to set expectations right, because Khao Kho Tree Top is a small place that doesn't have a big restaurant or a buffet breakfast like the larger resorts · The point many people mention is the moo kratha (Thai BBQ) service, eaten in a relaxed way on the balcony in the cool air, which is a popular activity for a Khao Kho stay in the cool season · There's also an affiliated café called Moss View Café across the road, as foreign reviews note — but with a caveat from the real reviews that walking to the café in the evening means walking in the dark, so "you should bring a flashlight or use your phone light" because the path isn't very well lit · For other meals, since the place doesn't have a full restaurant, most people choose to drive out to find eateries in the Khao Kho zone, or bring their own food to eat in the room and on the balcony · The upside of being a small place is the homey, friendly feel, but the trade-off is that you have to plan meals yourself more than at a big resort · Anyone who wants dinner to be easy, we'd suggest asking the property in advance whether there's a moo kratha or food service during your stay, because a small place may need advance booking at certain times

Service — for a small place like this, service is usually run by the owner or a small team, which comes with both upsides and caveats · The upside is a homey, informal, friendly feel, and many people say they got a warm welcome · But from the real reviews, cleanliness and service score middling in some reviews, reflecting that the standard may not be as consistent as at resorts with a dedicated professional team · This is a general trait of small hillside places run hands-on, rather than a serious flaw · What helps is contacting the property directly before you travel to confirm your booking, ask about the route up the hill, and check whether food service is available during your stay · The contact numbers found in the property information are 098-235-2838 and 088-323-1323 · Overall, if you set your expectations at "a small budget-friendly place," the service counts as decent and friendly — just don't expect big-hotel service

Real guest reviews (both good and bad) — gathered from booking sites and international review sites like Tripadvisor and Booking.com, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: the valley and ridge views from the balcony are lovely and the main selling point, the air is pleasantly cool especially on nights that are just-right cold with thick blankets to stay warm, the location is near Khao Kho attractions like Pha Sorn Kaew and the mosaic temple, and the price counts as good value for a sleep-with-a-view on the hills · Some foreign reviews rate comfort and location as good · On the caveats side: what gets mentioned is that the signs are all in Thai, making it hard for foreign visitors to find the way in, and the place is farther from the mosaic temple than expected, that walking to Moss View Café in the evening means walking in the dark so you should bring a flashlight, that all the room types are alike apart from upper vs. lower floor, and that cleanliness and service score middling in some reviews · On international review sites, the place scores around 4 out of 5 and sits among the province's mid-ranked niche stays · In short, most of the complaints are things you can manage by setting expectations right and preparing in advance, rather than problems that put people off coming

"The cabin is simple but the view is worth so much — you can sip coffee on the balcony watching the valley all morning · What I'd warn about is that the road up is a mountain road, the signs are in Thai, and it's pretty dark at night. If you're heading out to eat, bring a flashlight and drive carefully."

Price comparison and value — Khao Kho Tree Top positions itself among the budget-friendly Khao Kho stays, where on international booking sites the budget options in the Khao Kho zone usually start at around 1,200–1,500 baht a night (about $37 and up per review-site data) in normal pricing, rising during the cool-season high season when crowds flock up Khao Kho to see the sea of mist · Compared with all-out themed resorts on Khao Kho, such as English-style or design resorts starting at 2,500 baht and up into the many thousands, Khao Kho Tree Top is clearly cheaper and suits people paying for "the view and the air" rather than "the luxury" · So the value here depends on what you care about — if you value sleeping with a valley in view on a budget and aren't fussed about luxury or amenities, this is great value · But if you expect a beautiful room, a pool, and full service, paying more to stay at a big resort may be better value in terms of the overall experience · Another thing that helps with value is that small places like this tend to have steadier prices and can be negotiable at certain times; try comparing prices on Agoda and Booking.com, or ask the property directly before deciding

Things to know before booking — there are several things that help make a stay at Khao Kho Tree Top smoother · One, you should drive yourself and allow extra time for the drive up; if you come in the rainy season drive carefully because the road can be slippery, and pin the resort's name accurately in your navigation app because most signs are in Thai · Two, the best window is the late rainy/early cool season (October–February) when the air is cool and there's a chance to see the sea of mist in the valley in the morning — but it's the high season when rooms fill fast and prices climb, so book ahead · Three, bring warm clothes because the nights on the hillside are genuinely cold; reviews agree blankets are provided but you should bring a jacket as backup · Four, plan your meals in advance because the small place doesn't have a full restaurant — ask about the moo kratha service or bring your own food, and if you're heading out to a café or shop in the evening bring a flashlight · Five, contact the property directly to confirm your booking, the route, and the services during your stay, especially if you book off the main platforms · Six, set your expectations at "a small, simple, good-view, budget-friendly place" from the start, and the experience will match what you get as closely as possible

Summary — from all the real reviews, Khao Kho Tree Top is the place that suits best for people who want to sleep with a valley view and breathe the cool air on Khao Kho on a budget without being fussed about luxury or a full set of amenities · Its strengths are the valley and ridge views from the balcony, cool air almost year-round, a location near Pha Sorn Kaew and the Khao Kho attractions, and a price that's lower than many all-out themed resorts · What you have to make peace with is that it's a small, simple place, the rooms aren't luxurious, there's no pool or full restaurant, the signs are in Thai, the route is an uphill mountain road, and cleanliness and service score middling in some reviews · If you're after a luxury resort with a pool and full service, this may not be your answer, and you should consider the larger, higher-priced resorts on Khao Kho · But for a Khao Kho road trip where you want "a view worth the price" and the feel of a quiet cabin in the mountains — Khao Kho Tree Top is a budget option that delivers a simple, restful stay that's good for the money you pay

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Khao Kho Tree Top

faq.q: Where is Khao Kho Tree Top · how do you get there?
faq.a: It's located at No. 216, Khao Kho subdistrict, Khao Kho district, Phetchabun province, on a hillside facing the valley · It's near Wat Phra Borommathat Kanchanaphisek (the mosaic temple), about 2 km away, and Wat Pha Sorn Kaew · It suits driving yourself because the route is an uphill climb and most signs are in Thai, so pin it accurately in your navigation app

faq.q: What's the starting price at Khao Kho Tree Top · what room types are there?
faq.a: It's a budget-friendly place, starting at about ฿1,200/night in normal periods · There are twin rooms, triple rooms, and cabins (bungalows) facing the valley · Most rooms use fans and have a sitting balcony and an en-suite bathroom · In the cool-season high season prices climb and rooms fill fast, so book ahead

faq.q: Does Khao Kho Tree Top have breakfast or a swimming pool?
faq.a: It's a small place with no swimming pool and no buffet breakfast like the bigger resorts · There's a moo kratha (Thai BBQ) service to enjoy on the balcony in the cool air, and an affiliated Moss View Café across the road · We'd suggest asking the property in advance about food service during your stay, and planning your own dinner

faq.q: Who is Khao Kho Tree Top right for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for couples, small families, and nature lovers who want to sleep with a valley view on a budget and aren't fussed about luxury · You get a mountain view, cool air, and a location near the Khao Kho attractions · If you're after a luxury resort with a pool and full service, the larger, higher-priced resorts on Khao Kho may suit you better

faq.q: When is the best time to stay at Khao Kho Tree Top?
faq.a: The best window is the late rainy/early cool season (October–February), when the air is pleasantly cool and there's a chance to see the sea of mist drifting through the valley in the morning · It's Khao Kho's high season, so rooms fill fast and prices climb — book ahead and bring warm clothes too

faq.q: Are there any things to watch out for before staying?
faq.a: From the real reviews: the signs are in Thai, making the way in hard to find especially at night, the path in the evening is fairly dark so bring a flashlight, the route is an uphill mountain road that can be slippery in the rain, and cleanliness and service score middling in some reviews · Set your expectations at a small, simple, good-view, budget-friendly place, and it'll match what you get as closely as possible
